messages.subject: [Bioc-devel] Apply for the 2027 Bioconductor Developers Mentorship Program!
messages.subject_clean: [Bioc-devel] Apply for the 2027 Bioconductor Developers Mentorship Program!
messages.body_plain:
✨The Bioconductor Developers Mentorship Program is back! ✨

Following a successful round in 2022 (iykyk), The Student-ECR Council is
reviving the mentorship program to bring together developers of the
Bioconductor community! Read more about us here
<https://blog.bioconductor.org/posts/2026-08-06-student-ecr-intro/>.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Do you have a computational tool and you’re not sure how to turn it into a
Bioconductor package?

Do you have previous experience with package development and would like to
pass on your knowledge to the next generation of developers?

This is the program for you! 😄

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Over the course of 6 months, mentees will learn the *fundamentals of
developing a user-friendly and robust package* and/or *submit a candidate
package* to the Bioconductor/Contributions
<https://github.com/Bioconductor/Contributions> GitHub repository with
sufficient advance for review ahead of the following release deadline.
Mentee/mentors will split into small groups and meet over zoom to discuss
various aspects of package development and receive personalised feedback.

*Time commitment for mentors:* Zoom meeting 1h/month. Responding to Zulip
messages outside of meetings is up to the capacity of the individual mentor.

*Time commitment for mentees:* Zoom meeting 1h/month and taking the time
necessary to consistently improve upon the package and actioning feedback.

We are now taking applications for the incoming round: *April 2027 -
October 2027*! 🥳 More information is in the application forms below -

Application form for mentees: https://forms.gle/7kcExTASL8vcTDhr5

Application form for mentors: https://forms.gle/m14YEg1BRbDjBWos5

The deadline to apply is *24 November 2026*. If you have any questions,
please feel free to message in the #student-ecr Zulip channel. Applicants
will be informed of their outcome in February/March 2027.

We hope to see many of you apply! On behalf of the Student-ECR Council,

Carissa

messages.subject: [Bioc-devel] Waiting for new package review
messages.body_plain:
Hi Apratim,

Thank you for your package submission and your patience. As you say, package reviews are done by volunteers and there are a lot of packages in the queue. Your package assignee currently has 6 packages ahead of yours in their queue at this time of writing (github.com/Bioconductor/BiocContributions/issues?q=is%3Aissue+state%3Aopen+assignee%3Ahyu-kim) so a three-week turnaround from submission to review isn't something we can realistically expect. We do our best to get to every submission in the order it was received, but timing depends on reviewer availability.

If you'd like to help speed things up we are always looking for more reviewers. Reviewing is a great way to learn the project's standards and every additional reviewer shortens the wait for everyone, including you, on future submissions. Details on getting involved are here: contributions.bioconductor.org/review-volunteer-chapter.html

Bioconductor is built and maintained by people who give their time freely and the project works best when those who are able also contribute back where they can.

Pariksheet

Pariksheet Nanda, PhD
Postdoctoral Associate
Shoemaker Laboratory
Department of Chemical Engineering
University of Pittsburgh

messages.subject_clean: [Bioc-devel] ChemmineOB devl failing on windows x86_64
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kevin,

Sorry for the delay getting back to you.

R Universe uses GitHub actions and GitHub's standard runners,<https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners> so we can no longer install system requirements for maintainers.

There are a few ways to deal with system requirements in R Universe for Windows (and macosx).

Where appropriate, it could be bundled with Rtools for Windows and a macosx recipe could be made available at https://github.com/r-macos/recipes. I recommend submitting a recipe for ChemmineOB system requirements. However, Rtools is currently frozen.

Another approach to produce working Windows and macosx binaries is to vendor system requirements, either in the package itself, like Rgraphviz, or in a separate companion package, like Rhtslib/Rsamtools and Rhdf5lib/rhdf5. A separate companion package separates the requirement to a single install that can guarantee compatibility with ChemmineOB for that release. (Thanks to Herv? for this suggestion.) This might be a good approach for ChemmineOB and I recommend looking at those packages.

You might also consider using an agent to facilitate vendoring the system requirements. I also recommend using the R Universe GitHub Action<https://docs.r-universe.dev/bioconductor/#testing-the-build-in-your-own-ci> to test the build. It's easy to set up, runs all the same jobs and on its summary page, the action collects the binaries it produces, which you can download and test.

Given the effort involved and other constraints, you may decide to drop support for an operating system, which you can specify with `Config/Bioconductor/UnsupportedPlatforms<https://contributions.bioconductor.org/advanced-build-options.html?q=unsupp#skipping-builds-on-unsupported-platforms>` in your DESCRIPTION file.

Andres Wokaty (they/them)

Waldron Lab at CUNY SPH
Bioconductor Core Team

messages.subject: [Bioc-devel]  Private report: ancestrymap SNP-name buffer overflow in LEA
messages.subject_clean: [Bioc-devel]  Private report: ancestrymap SNP-name buffer overflow in LEA
messages.body_plain:
Dear Hong, 

Thank you very much for reporting the buffer overflow vulnerability in LEA and for providing a reproducible example. 

We confirmed the issue and identified a second vulnerable code path in the ANCESTRYMAP conversion routines. Both have now been fixed, and the corrections have passed regression tests and AddressSanitizer checks. 

The fix has been committed and pushed to the Bioconductor development branch (LEA 3.25.1) and is also available on GitHub (bcm-uga/LEA). 

We have also prepared and validated a backport for the current release branch (`RELEASE_3_23`, LEA 3.24.1). However, the push to Bioconductor was rejected with the following message: 

`remote: FATAL: W refs/heads/RELEASE_3_23 packages/LEA olivier.francois DENIED by fallthru` 

To the Bioconductor team (cc): Could you please advise on the appropriate procedure for publishing this security fix to the release branch, or whether additional write permissions are required? 

We are also reviewing related input-validation issues in other conversion routines. 

Thank you again Hong, for bringing this issue to our attention. 

Best regards, 

Olivier François 



De: "Qin, Hong" <hqin at odu.edu> 
À: "Olivier Francois" <olivier.francois at grenoble-inp.fr> 
Envoyé: Mardi 10 Novembre 2026 06:12:15 
Objet: Private report: ancestrymap SNP-name buffer overflow in LEA 



Hello Olivier Francois, 

I am writing to alert you to an ancestrymap name-buffer overflow in LEA identified during our source-verification study. 

We used OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude for source analysis, reproduction harnesses, and review of saved test results. Claude designed and ran the static scan; Codex and Claude assisted with verification and source and log audits. 

In version 3.23.0 (Git revision f812da2d3aae5456f0f17776f6ea64fd1de91e88 ), read_line_ancestrymap copies the SNP-name field with strcpy into a 512-byte buffer at src/convert/ancestrymap.c:160. Input lines can occupy a larger, 1,000-byte buffer. A saved AddressSanitizer test with a 600-character name records a stack-buffer overflow with a 601-byte write. 

Testing built the package native sources, ran the initializer, and invoked the registered .C entry R_ancestrymap2geno. An unchanged-source adapter reproduced the same copy error. The complete installed-package R workflow has not been tested. 

Source comparisons found the relevant native source unchanged in development version 3.25.0 and inspected release versions 3.22.0 and 3.24.0. 

Best regards, 
Hong Qin 
Old Dominion University

messages.subject: [Bioc-devel] Package review is a lottery: BiocContributions queue numbers
messages.subject_clean: [Bioc-devel] Package review is a lottery: BiocContributions queue numbers
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

How long a new Bioconductor package waits depends less on the code than 
on which reviewer it draws. From the full BiocContributions history 
(until today 12 Nov, 208 assignments):

- Median time to acceptance: 23 to 115 days, depending on the reviewer.
- Median time to first reviewer comment: 9 to 144 days.
- 58 open reviews are older than two months.
- New packages still go to reviewers holding 11 to 14 open reviews, 
while others hold 2 or 3.
- 6 packages have no reviewer at all, one since June.

I believe this is a design problem, not a people problem. Equal intake 
regardless of load means 17 separate queues at very different speeds 
(understandably each reviewer donates different amount of time and effort).

What I propose as a fix:
 ?- One shared queue; push new packages at the end for it; pop the front 
and assign to the next reviewer that has below a cap of open reviews 
(say 4).
 ?- If there is no reviewer comment within say 21 days, then the package 
goes back to the front of the queue.
 ?- Keep hand-picking for packages that need a specialist.
 ?- Publish queue sizes and response times.

We as contributors are expected to follow strict standards and 
deadlines. I believe reviews should meet the same bar. Happy to help 
build this into the workflow.

Best,

-- 
Anestis Gkanogiannis, PhD
----------
Independent Researcher / Bioinformatics & AI Consultant
PhD in Machine Learning, Athens University of Economics and Business
Github: github.com/gkanogiannis
Linkedin: linkedin.com/in/anestis-gkanogiannis

messages.subject: [Bioc-devel] org.Hs.eg.db and KEGG pathways
messages.body_plain:
Hi list,

Recently, I received a notification that my package was failing the build
on devel.
The error comes from the object at org.Hs.eg.db::org.Hs.egPATH having a
long list of NA:

packageVersion("org.Hs.eg.db")
## [1] '3.24.4'
all(vapply(org.Hs.eg.db::org.Hs.egPATH, is.na, TRUE))
## [1] TRUE

The object contained some data related to KEGG which restricted access to
its database.

It is a suggested package and I can work around the issue but I thought I
would check before I go down this route if this will be fixed on the
org.Hs.eg.db package or not.

Many thanks to Bioconductor for maintaining it,
Cheers,

Lluís

PS: I'm not sure if some other packages are affected by this update.
